blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *   jobParams.validationConcurrency (default 1, gh-837) — parallel-validation knob:
 *     the ai_validating/pr_approved merge-window mutex admits up to N CONCURRENT
 *     approved-arm validations (repo-var analog; .dmtools/config.js
 *     smValidationConcurrency overrides, clamped to 5). The effective concurrency
 *     rises from 1 to the knob only when the approved queue depth is at/above
 *     jobParams.validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark (default 3) — below it the
 *     window stays strictly serial (runner-budget protection; knob 1 = unchanged
 *     legacy behavior). jobParams.validationMinutesEstimate (default 35) feeds the
 *     per-tick validation-minutes runner-cost report (AC2, hard-capped at
 *     concurrency x estimate).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket},
 *                               {status.KEY[:Literal]} and {stage.KEY[:Literal]}, see configLoader)
 *   jqlByTracker   (optional) — { ado: '<WIQL>', github: '<query>' }: the query for that tracker replaces
 *                               `jql` (a project on ADO supplies native WIQL without forking sm.json)
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering
 *   workflowFile   (optional) — GitHub Actions workflow file  (default: ai-teammate.yml)
 *   workflowRef    (optional) — git ref for dispatch           (default: main)
 *   concurrencyKey (optional) — workflow concurrency key override (default: ticket key)
 *   projectKey     (optional) — value passed as the `project_key` workflow input so the runner
 *                               activates the correct project-specific dependency setup (e.g. "myproject",
 *                               "bice"). Auto-derived from configPath basename when not set
 *                               (e.g. ".dmtools/configs/myproject.js" → "myproject").
 *   skipIfLabel    (optional) — skip ticket if it already has this label (idempotency)
 *   skipIfLabels   (optional) — skip ticket if it already has any of these labels
 *   addLabel       (optional) — add this label after triggering (idempotency marker)
 *   addLabels      (optional) — add these labels after triggering
 *   recoverStaleTriggerLabel (optional) — if true, remove skip labels when no matching

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *   jobParams.validationConcurrency (default 1, gh-837) — parallel-validation knob:
 *     the ai_validating/pr_approved merge-window mutex admits up to N CONCURRENT
 *     approved-arm validations (repo-var analog; .dmtools/config.js
 *     smValidationConcurrency overrides, clamped to 5). The effective concurrency
 *     rises from 1 to the knob only when the approved queue depth is at/above
 *     jobParams.validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark (default 3) — below it the
 *     window stays strictly serial (runner-budget protection; knob 1 = unchanged
 *     legacy behavior). jobParams.validationMinutesEstimate (default 35) feeds the
 *     per-tick validation-minutes runner-cost report (AC2, hard-capped at
 *     concurrency x estimate).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket},
 *                               {status.KEY[:Literal]} and {stage.KEY[:Literal]}, see configLoader)
 *   jqlByTracker   (optional) — { ado: '<WIQL>', github: '<query>' }: the query for that tracker replaces
 *                               `jql` (a project on ADO supplies native WIQL without forking sm.json)
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *   jobParams.validationConcurrency (default 1, gh-837) — parallel-validation knob:
 *     the ai_validating/pr_approved merge-window mutex admits up to N CONCURRENT
 *     approved-arm validations (repo-var analog; .dmtools/config.js
 *     smValidationConcurrency overrides, clamped to 5). The effective concurrency
 *     rises from 1 to the knob only when the approved queue depth is at/above
 *     jobParams.validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark (default 3) — below it the
 *     window stays strictly serial (runner-budget protection; knob 1 = unchanged
 *     legacy behavior). jobParams.validationMinutesEstimate (default 35) feeds the
 *     per-tick validation-minutes runner-cost report (AC2, hard-capped at
 *     concurrency x estimate).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket},
 *                               {status.KEY[:Literal]} and {stage.KEY[:Literal]}, see configLoader)
 *   jqlByTracker   (optional) — { ado: '<WIQL>', github: '<query>' }: the query for that tracker replaces
 *                               `jql` (a project on ADO supplies native WIQL without forking sm.json)
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).
 *   jobParams.validationConcurrency (default 1, gh-837) — parallel-validation knob:
 *     the ai_validating/pr_approved merge-window mutex admits up to N CONCURRENT
 *     approved-arm validations (repo-var analog; .dmtools/config.js
 *     smValidationConcurrency overrides, clamped to 5). The effective concurrency
 *     rises from 1 to the knob only when the approved queue depth is at/above
 *     jobParams.validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark (default 3) — below it the
 *     window stays strictly serial (runner-budget protection; knob 1 = unchanged
 *     legacy behavior). jobParams.validationMinutesEstimate (default 35) feeds the
 *     per-tick validation-minutes runner-cost report (AC2, hard-capped at
 *     concurrency x estimate).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket},
 *                               {status.KEY[:Literal]} and {stage.KEY[:Literal]}, see configLoader)
 *   jqlByTracker   (optional) — { ado: '<WIQL>', github: '<query>' }: the query for that tracker replaces
 *                               `jql` (a project on ADO supplies native WIQL without forking sm.json)
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that

 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.

- Require reworkLoopGuard.

 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,

 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)

 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):

 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel

But the gh-957 ticket says the loop guard should be: "N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment)". The existing emptyLapMax guard covers red-gated rework arms via fail_validation, but the gh-957 case is the threads-armed rework (unresolved review threads), where legs return "success" with no push and no resolution, and the arm rule keeps re-arming (arm_rework fires whenever threadsResolved:false).

The restore_rework_arm sweep (gh-840) restores the arm when consumption left threads unresolved after 30 min stale... Actually the re-arm comments "🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed" every cycle — that's the arm_rework rule firing, which requires notLabels agent:rework. The label gets consumed on dispatch (consumeLabels), then the arm rule fires again next tick? The arm_rework rule has no stale gate — it fires whenever PR is reviewed+ai_pr_reviewed with unresolved threads and no label. So: arm → dispatch consumes label → leg runs (no-op) → next tick arm fires again. That's the loop. The gh-840 restore sweep has a 30-min stale bound, but the direct arm_rework rule has no bound.

So the loop guard needed: track consecutive no-op rework legs on the same head (zero pushed commits AND zero resolved threads) and after N, stop arming + escalate. There's already an `emptyLapMax` guard (fail_validation withholds arm after N empty rework laps on same head). But the gh-957 ticket says the loop guard should be: "N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment)". The existing emptyLapMax guard covers red-gated rework arms via fail_validation, but the gh-957 case is the threads-armed rework (unresolved review threads), where legs return "success" with no push and no resolution, and the arm rule keeps re-arming (arm_rework fires whenever threadsResolved:false).

Wait — but how did it re-arm 7 times if the rework-on-label rule consumes the label on dispatch? Actually the re-arm comments "🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed" every cycle — that's the arm_rework rule firing, which requires notLabels agent:rework. The label gets consumed on dispatch (consumeLabels), then the arm rule fires again next tick? The arm_rework rule has no stale gate — it fires whenever PR is reviewed+ai_pr_reviewed with unresolved threads and no label. So: arm → dispatch consumes label → leg runs (no-op) → next tick arm fires again. That's the loop. The gh-840 restore sweep has a 30-min stale bound, but the direct arm_rework rule has no bound.

So the loop guard needed: track consecutive no-op rework legs on the same head (zero pushed commits AND zero resolved threads) and after N, stop arming + escalate. There's an existing "empty lap" concept tied to fail_validation/red markers (🔴 red-head markers). The gh-957 fix should probably record a marker from the rework leg's post-action (pushReworkChanges) when the lap was a no-op (no commit pushed, no threads resolved), and the arm_rework action consults it, withholding at N consecutive on same head and escalating.

I now have a good picture of the existing machinery. Given the enormous scope, let me define a concrete, implementable plan aligned with the ticket's three required fixes:

**Fix 1 — same-source thread list for the rework leg.**
The arm rule counts GraphQL reviewThreads with `isResolved === false`. The leg's `fetchDiscussions` (scm.js + githubHelpers.js) builds its thread list from `github_get_pr_conversations` and only *enriches* with GraphQL ids. In the live incident the conversations export surfaced only 2 threads (dropped as notices) while GraphQL counted 64. 

Fix: when the GraphQL reviewThreads fetch succeeds, the thread list should be built from the GraphQL nodes themselves (which carry id, isResolved, path, line, root comment author/body, databaseId), unioned/matched with conversations for reply bodies. The key change: enumerate threads from `github_get_pr_review_threads` nodes (isResolved=false count matches the armer), not from conversations. Each GraphQL node has comments.nodes[0] with databaseId + author + body. So we can build rawThreads from GraphQL nodes directly, falling back to the conversations path when GraphQL is unavailable.

Where to implement: `js/common/scm.js` fetchDiscussions (github provider) and `js/common/githubHelpers.js` fetchDiscussionsAndRawData. Both have near-duplicate logic. Better: implement once in a shared pure-ish helper... githubHelpers is required by scm? Let me check: does scm.js require githubHelpers? Probably not (circular risk). I'll implement a shared helper module `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js` (pure: takes GraphQL nodes + conversations, returns rawThreads + markdown) used by both. Hmm, but the markdown building differs slightly (const vs var etc.). Both build the same markdown. Let me check whether scm.js has access to machineNotice — yes it uses machineNotice.isMachineNoticeBody.

Plan for Fix 1:
- New module `js/common/reviewThreads.js` (pure): `buildThreadInventory(graphqlNodes, conversations)` → { threads: [...], markdown, counts }. GraphQL-first enumeration: for each node → thread entry {threadId, rootCommentId, resolved, bot, author, body, path, line}; supplement body/author from conversation match by rootCommentId when GraphQL first comment lacks body (pagination). Then markdown from open non-bot non-notice threads.
- Use it in scm.js fetchDiscussions and githubHelpers.fetchDiscussionsAndRawData.

Wait — but do GraphQL nodes include the *body* of the root comment? In smProvider.reviewThreadList they read `first.body` and `first.author` from t.comments.nodes[0], so yes the dmtools `github_get_pr_review_threads` global returns nodes with comments.nodes[0].{databaseId,author,body,path?...}. And path/line come from node t.path, t.line. OK.

Also review_state.md in preCliReworkSetup: it lists open threads from `discussionData.rawThreads.threads` — once rawThreads is GraphQL-sourced, review_state.md automatically matches the arm count. Good — that satisfies "thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts". I should also make review_state.md show the total open count matching GraphQL (including notices/bots? The arm counts ALL unresolved threads regardless of author). Hmm — the arm rule counts every unresolved thread (reviewThreads.unresolved). The leg's actionable list excludes bots and notices. That's fine as long as the count discrepancy is explained. But the ticket says: leg concluded "Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix" because the thread list was wrong. With GraphQL-first enumeration, all 64 threads would be listed. 64 threads can't all fit... well, they can be listed as bullets.

Actually wait — also check: does the arm rule count machine-authored threads only? The `restore_rework_arm` sweep counts *machine* unresolved threads; but the main arm_rework rule matches on `threadsResolved:false` — computed where? Let me check how `threadsResolved` gets into the ticket record for the github query rules. Search for threadsResolved in smAgent/smProvider.

Read the error logs in that file carefully (last 500 lines; full logs are in `ci_failures_full.log`) to identify the root cause, then fix the code. So `openInputThreads.length > 0` was false → the guard didn't fire → the leg completed "successfully" with zero work → threads stay open → arm rule re-arms next tick. That's the exact mechanism.

So the three fixes hang together:

**Fix 1 (context parity):** make the leg's thread inventory GraphQL-sourced (same as `provider.reviewThreads` count). This fixes the root mismatch: the leg will SEE the 64 open threads in pr_discussions.md / pr_discussions_raw.json / review_state.md.

**Fix 2 (audit resolve):** when the leg determines all open threads are addressed/invalid (no code changes needed), it must be able to resolve them with an explanatory reply per thread, including the rework run URL. Currently the agents#827 guard blocks ANY no-code-change completion with open threads (moves to Blocked). The ticket says: "A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL)."

Now the loop guard (Fix 3). Where does the SM re-arm? The `arm_rework` action in smAgent.js fires whenever the PR matches: unresolved threads (GraphQL count > 0), notLabels agent:rework, reviewed, etc. The rework-on-label rule dispatches and consumes the label; the no-op leg finishes 'success' (no push, no resolution); next tick arm_rework fires again → infinite loop.

Existing guards:
- emptyLapMax — tied to fail_validation red markers, only for red-gate arms.
- restore_rework_arm (gh-840) — has a stale-grace, but that's a different path (arm consumed without leg).
- The arm latch (gh-806) — one arm per (pr, head) while a leg is in flight. Doesn't help after leg completes.

Fix 3 design: the rework post-action records an audit marker on the PR per leg close: `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap {head, pushed: N, resolved: N, at} -->` (machine identity–keyed? markers parsed from PR comments... existing marker readers parse bodies without author gating in failMarkerState, but reworkConsumption parses with authorLogins allowlist). For safety, follow reworkConsumption's forge-hardening: author allowlist.

The arm_rework action then reads these lap markers (one comment fetch — can reuse? arm_rework currently does not fetch comments; reworkArmGate reads verdict records via provider.latestVerdictRecord which fetches comments... it uses ioCache so probably the same fetch is cached? Not necessarily).

Design decision — new pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js`:
- `buildLapMarker(headSha, pushedCommits, resolvedThreads, runUrl, atIso)` → marker comment body (hidden HTML comment + visible escalation-safe line? No — the marker should be quiet: just the HTML comment; but we also want an explanatory PR comment? The post action already posts completion comments. Keep the marker minimal).

## Implementation plan

### New module: `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (pure)
- `NOOP_LAP_MARKER_PREFIX = '<!-- dmtools:rework-lap '`
- `buildLapMarker(headSha, pushed, resolved, atIso)` → marker line (`<!-- dmtools:rework-lap {"head":..., "pushed":0|1, "resolved":N, "at":...} -->`) + short visible line for greppability.
- `parseLapMarkers(comments, opts)` — author-allowlist-gated, sorted by atMs (reuse pattern from reworkConsumption).
- `consecutiveNoopLaps(markers, headSha)` — newest-first run of markers with same head && pushed===0 && resolved===0; stops at first non-matching marker (progress lap or different head).
- `shouldWithholdReworkArm(state)` — state: {markers, headSha, maxNoopLaps, escalationPosted} → {withhold, laps, escalate}.
- `ESCALATION_MARKER_PREFIX` / `buildEscalationMarker(headSha, laps, atIso)` + `parseEscalationMarkers` for once-per-head dedup.
- `ESCALATION_LABEL = 'rework-loop-escalated'`.
- `buildEscalationComment(headSha, laps)` — the 🛑 owner comment.

### smAgent.js changes
- Require reworkLoopGuard.
- New jobParams knob: `noopLapMax` (default 2) with accessor `noopLapMaxOf(jobParams)` (pattern like emptyLapMaxOf/redHeadCapOf).

content.text:
You are performing a focused rework of code based on Pull Request review feedback.

## Your Primary Goal

Fix **every issue** raised in `pr_discussions.md`. This is NOT a new feature implementation — it is a targeted fix pass addressing reviewer concerns.

## Merge Conflicts (resolve before anything else)

If `merge_conflicts.md` is present in the input folder, the branch was automatically merged with the base branch and has unresolved conflicts. You **must** resolve them first:

1. Check which files have conflict markers: look at `merge_conflicts.md` or run `git status --short`
2. For each conflicting file, open it and resolve every `<<<<<<<` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` block — keep the correct/merged content
3. Stage each resolved file: `git add <file>`
4. Verify no markers remain: `git diff --check`
5. Only after all conflicts are staged, proceed to the review fixes below

Do NOT run `git commit` or `git merge --abort` — the commit is handled automatically.

## Approach

1. **Read `pr_discussions.md` first** — list all review comments and threads before touching any code
2. **Be surgical but thorough** — before opening or editing any source file, run `codegraph context "<ticket key> <review issue and affected area>"`, even if the review already names an exact file, line, failing assertion, or test. Then fix the exact issue the reviewer flagged and use CodeGraph to find the same structural pattern across the codebase. Use `codegraph query`, `codegraph callers`, or `codegraph impact` when you know a symbol. Use `grep` only after CodeGraph when you need a literal string search. This prevents the same issue from being raised in the next review cycle. Do not refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features.
3. **Address BLOCKING issues first** (security, critical bugs), then IMPORTANT, then SUGGESTIONS
4. **If a SUGGESTION is minor and time-consuming**, you may skip it but explicitly note it in `outputs/response.md`

## Scope-Creep Review Loop Guard

If a reviewer blocks the PR because `pr_diff.txt` contains an unrelated deleted file, generated/cache artifact, tooling file, or other out-of-scope path, this is an actionable blocking issue even if it appears as a general PR comment instead of an inline thread.

Before writing a no-action response:
- Re-read `pr_diff.txt` and confirm the blocked path is no longer present.
- For deleted unrelated files, restore the file from the base branch or otherwise remove that deletion from the PR diff.
- Do not write "No open review comments" or "No new actionable items" while the blocked path remains in `pr_diff.txt`.
- If the same path appears in repeated review cycles, fix that path first to stop the loop.

## Rework Decision Flow

Use this flow before changing code so approved PRs that are only waiting for CI or merge checks do not enter a stale rework loop:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start PR rework] --> B{rework_setup_failed.md exists?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Write setup failure response and empty replies]
    B -->|No| D{merge_conflicts.md exists?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Resolve conflicts first]
    D -->|No| F{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?}
    E --> F
    F -->|Yes| G[Fix CI root cause — use ci_failures.md (last 500 lines) and ci_failures_full.log (full logs)]
    F -->|No| H{pr_discussions.md has open actionable items?}
    G --> H
    H -->|Yes| I[Fix every thread and write matching replies]
    H -->|No| J{Only waiting for fresh review, checks, or merge?}
    J -->|Yes| K[Write no-action response and empty replies]
    J -->|No| L[Write no-open-review-comments response]
    I --> M[Run relevant checks]
    M --> N[Write outputs/response.md and outputs/review_replies.json]
    K --> N
    L --> N
```

====
12:9. `merge_conflicts.md` *(if present)* — **Merge conflicts that MUST be resolved FIRST** before any rework
14:11. `pr_discussions.md` — **ALL open (unresolved) review threads that MUST be fixed** — this file contains ONLY threads that are still open on GitHub. Already-resolved threads are excluded. **Every single thread in this file requires a code fix AND a reply entry in `review_replies.json` — no exceptions.**
20:**If `merge_conflicts.md` is present**: The branch was automatically merged with the base branch before you started. There are unresolved conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) in the listed files. **Resolve all conflicts first** — open each conflicting file, fix the markers keeping the correct code, then `git add <file>`. Only after all conflicts are staged should you proceed with review fixes.
22:**If `ci_failures.md` is present**: CI checks are currently failing on this PR. Read the error logs in that file carefully (last 500 lines; full logs are in `ci_failures_full.log`) to identify the root cause, then fix the code. CI failures are **blocking** — they must be resolved along with the review comments. After pushing, CI will re-run automatically.
51:If `pr_discussions.md` contains NO actionable items (no human review threads AND no automated test failures/warnings), then there is **nothing to fix** — write a short `outputs/response.md` stating "No open review comments to address" and an empty `outputs/review_replies.json` (`{ "replies": [] }`), then exit. **Do NOT post multiple acknowledgment comments.**
57:    A[Inspect PR context] --> B{Open unresolved review threads?}
126:- NEVER use closing keywords (`closes #N`, `fixes #N`, `resolves #N`) in commit messages. Issue-closing keywords belong to the PR body; the squash-merge message owns closing the issue. A premature keyword auto-closes the issue before the fix is validated and merged.
