{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract

- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

## Summary

**Root cause**: the SM threads-rule arm re-armed a dev leg every ~10 min for 2h because the leg saw 2 review threads while the rework sweep's inventory counted 64 — the completion gate never passed, every leg closed "successful" with zero pushes and zero resolutions, and the threads-armed path had no empty-lap bound (the existing cap only covered the red-gate arm).

**Fix**:
- **`js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`** (new): GraphQL `reviewThreads`-first thread inventory, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and arm-rule census now the same source; the census rides into `pr_discussions_raw.json` (gitOps) and the `pr_discussions.md` section.
- **`js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js`** (new, pure): per-leg-close lap markers (hidden, machine-author-gated `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->`), consecutive-no-op counting, withhold decision; `pushReworkChanges` stamps one marker per close.
- **`js/smAgent.js`**: `arm_rework` **and** `restore_rework_arm` withhold at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head, escalating once per head (`rework-loop-escalated` label + 🛑 comment); a progress lap or new head resets the budget by construction.
- **Contract**: rework prompt/instructions updated (never write "No open review comments", audit-resolve path for already-addressed threads); `node_testRunner` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for GraalJS parity.
- **Tests**: 2 new suites (28 tests) + 4 new smAgent wiring tests + census tests in test_gitOps + require-map pins in test_reworkCustomParams/test_smAgent.
